newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Foreign firms to modernise Bulgaria reactors.
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms to modernise Bulgaria reactors.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG, France's Framatome, U.S.-based Westinghouse Electric Corp and Russian experts will modernise Bulgaria's two Soviet-made reactors, the energy ministry said on Wednesday.

"The projects for the future modernisation will be carried out by the Russian organisations -- designers and producers of VVER-1,000 reactors, Siemens, Framatome and Westinghouse, which are leaders in world's nuclear industry," a ministry statement said.
It added that a greater part of the reactors' modernisation would be performed by the consortium of Russian organisations, Siemens and Framatome.
The tender for the $250 million overhaul of the reactors included helping debt-ridden Bulgaria receive loans from international financial institutions to fund the modernisation.
The two 1,000-megawatt reactors are the largest and most modern units at the Kozloduy nuclear power plant.
Reactor number five has been in operation since 1987, while number six was licensed in December 1993 after a two-year commissioning period.
Apart from the two reactors, the Kozloduy plant has four 440-megawatt reactors and all six reactors meet more than 40 percent of the country's electricity needs.
